swartz-bay.blurb: The ferry waits at the dock. Cars and people get on for the next crossing.

lookout.title: Look out for cormorants
lookout.text: Black birds drying their wings on the posts near the dock

happening.title: Calm water at the terminal
happening.text: Swartz Bay is sheltered from wind and waves. The water near the dock mixes slowly, so the readings change very little until the ship leaves.

swanson-channel.blurb: Islands on both sides! Saltspring is to the west and the Penders are to the east.

lookout.title: Look out for orcas
lookout.text: Tall black fins travel through this channel in family groups

happening.title: Island water, mixed by the tide
happening.text: The channel is narrow and deep. Tidal currents move water between the islands, so temperature and salinity stay close to the values near Swartz Bay.

active-pass.blurb: Fast tides squeeze between Galiano and Mayne. Hold on, it can get bumpy!

lookout.title: Look out for harbour seals
lookout.text: Heads bobbing near the rocks on your left

happening.title: Tides are stirring the water column
happening.text: Strong currents through Active Pass mix deeper, colder water up toward the surface. Watch salinity dip slightly and turbidity rise until the ship reaches open water in the Strait of Georgia.

strait-of-georgia.blurb: Open water! In the middle, the strait is more than 400 m deep.

lookout.title: Look out for dolphins
lookout.text: White-sided dolphins sometimes leap in the waves beside the ship

happening.title: Deep, open water
happening.text: The strait is wide and deep. Away from the islands, fresh water from the Fraser River starts to spread across the top, so salinity falls slowly.

tsawwassen.blurb: Almost there! Muddy water from the Fraser River makes the sea look brown here.

lookout.title: Look out for herons
lookout.text: Great blue herons hunt in the shallow water near the causeway

happening.title: Fresh water on top
happening.text: The Fraser River pours fresh, muddy water into the strait. Salinity drops and turbidity rises as the ship comes near Tsawwassen.
